results.title: 7 AI Agents That Can Attend Your Meetings | Otter.ai
results.content:
Learn more

Two meetings overlap, but you still need a reliable record of what happens in the one you can’t attend. An AI agent can attend in your place. Passive notetakers summarize afterward, and active meeting participants answer questions mid-call, so you get the decisions without chasing colleagues for secondhand recaps.

Connect one to your calendar, and it joins as a participant to produce a searchable record of the conversation. Some stay silent and email a summary afterward, others answer questions live, and a few skip the bot entirely and capture audio from your device.

## The Short on Time Version [...] For example, MRI Software adopted Otter as an interconnected hub of knowledge for its sales engineering team. Searchable transcripts, summaries, and AI Chat replaced memory-based demo debriefs. The team saves 20 minutes per meeting and $150,000 annually, with ROI realized within 2.5 weeks of the pilot.

Try Otter free on your next meeting, or Get a demo to see the Meeting Agent on your calls.

## Frequently Asked Questions About AI Meeting Agents

### Can an AI Agent Join a Meeting Without Me?

Otter gives you the controls to configure the agent to join approved calendar meetings when you are unavailable or double-booked. It is your responsibility to disclose the agent, obtain the required permission, and confirm the host allows recording before the call begins. [...] #### Cons

 Users repeatedly cite inaccuracies in summarization and complex data tasks.
 Users highlight one tenant-scope limitation: Copilot only works for licensed users in your tenant and skips externally hosted meetings.

#### Pricing

Microsoft 365 Copilot is $30 per user per month paid yearly as an add-on to eligible Microsoft 365 plans. There is no free meeting-agent tier, though Copilot Chat is free.

#### Who Is Microsoft 365 Copilot For?

Copilot is for Microsoft organizations whose meetings stay within their tenant.

## Can an AI Really Attend a Meeting for You?

Before any of these tools joins a call on your behalf, the disclosure and consent question comes first, and the answer sits with you, not the vendor.
